# The step-budget repetition diagnostic is computed, then dropped

## Context / Problem

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a]. The reported symptom was "the gate cannot
be tuned because it cannot be observed" — no partial verdict, no count of anything, just a bare
budget number. The diagnostic that answers it **already exists** and is thrown away one frame from
the surface.

`interpret_failure` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:75-103`) builds `budget_diag` via
`usage_log.failure_usage`, which reduces every tool call to a `(tool_name, sha256(args)[:8])`
signature and summarizes it — `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`,
`top_repeated_tool_calls`. That is precisely the loop-vs-explore discriminator, and it is attached
as `budget_err.diagnostic`.

It then goes nowhere. `emit_gate_error` is only called by `raise_completion_workflow_failure` when
`failure_diagnostic` is truthy (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:373-403`), and
`failure_diagnostic` is set ONLY inside `CompletionAgentStep._recover` — which a budget exhaustion
never reaches (the sibling [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911] fixes reachability). So **no `gate_error_v1`
sidecar is written** and the CLI message carries none of it. In the instrumented reproduction the
propagated exception reached the caller with `diagnostic: null`.

Two operators burned ~50 minutes each escalating the budget 480 -> 1600 against a constraint that
was never a budget (and ticket 46a2-9c1a-d855-4706 records a third: 480 -> 1200, same result). The
measurement that would have said so in one line was computed on the first run and discarded.

## Approach

Wire the already-computed diagnostic through the two drops. First, `CompletionAgentStep` records the
caught exception's `.diagnostic` onto `self.failure_diagnostic` when it enters recovery (fd84 adds
the budget entry edge; this ticket makes the diagnostic it carries survive), so
`raise_completion_workflow_failure` — whose sidecar emission and `CompletionRecoveryError` path
already exist and are keyed on a truthy `failure_diagnostic` — emits the `gate_error_v1` sidecar
carrying the repetition counters. The carry path is NOT automatic: the caught exception's
`.diagnostic` is filtered through `_bounded_diagnostic`
(`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py`), whose `allowed` allowlist strips
`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls` and
`distinct_ratio_window` today — and whose scalar-only merge guard would drop the list-valued
`top_repeated_tool_calls` even if allowlisted. This ticket widens that allowlist with those four
repetition keys and relaxes the scalar-only guard for exactly `top_repeated_tool_calls` (a bounded
list of `{signature, count}` dicts — hashed signatures, no prompts or arguments), so the summary
survives both the recovery-exception merge and the `aggregate_*` primary-exception merge
([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed, established that carry). Second, the operator-facing
close-gate failure message renders the distinct-vs-total counts (via the existing
`usage_log.format_repetition` renderer, which already formats exactly these fields) so "it looped"
is distinguishable from "it ran out of room" without reading a log. No new computation: every value
is already produced by `usage_log.failure_usage`; this ticket widens the diagnostic filter to stop
dropping it and renders it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — `_bounded_diagnostic`: extend the `allowed`
  allowlist with `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`,
  `distinct_ratio_window`, and permit the list-typed `top_repeated_tool_calls` through `merge()`
  (all other keys stay scalar-only); include the repetition summary in the message
  `raise_completion_workflow_failure` raises.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` — the tests below.

Out of scope: making budget exhaustion reach this code at all ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed:
budget exhaustions now enter `_recover` and set `failure_diagnostic`); computing the detector's new
field ([rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0], landed: `failure_usage` now emits `distinct_ratio_window`).
This ticket carries both through the `_bounded_diagnostic` filter that currently strips them.

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py -q

Happy path: a budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails emits a `gate_error_v1` sidecar populated
with the repetition counters. Edge: a failure with NO diagnostic (the pre-existing bare path) still
raises `LLMError` exactly as today (regression-pinned). Privacy: the sidecar payload carries no
prompts, tool arguments, or response text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a step-budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails writes a `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying
      the repetition summary (`requests`, `tool_calls`, `tool_calls_distinct`,
      `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`, `distinct_ratio_window`) — i.e. the
      `_bounded_diagnostic` allowlist passes these keys and the list-valued
      `top_repeated_tool_calls` survives the merge; verified by a test asserting the sidecar is
      emitted and its counters are populated
- [ ] the operator-facing close-gate failure message includes the distinct-vs-total tool-call counts,
      so "it looped" is distinguishable from "it ran out of room" without reading a log; verified by
      a test asserting the raised error's message contains the counts
- [ ] the sidecar payload stays free of prompts, tool arguments and response text (the existing
      privacy contract in `usage_log.failure_usage` is preserved); verified by a test asserting only
      hashed signatures and counters appear
- [ ] a failure without any diagnostic still raises the current bare `LLMError` unchanged (no
      manufactured empty sidecar); regression-pinned by a test
